learningObjective: Reason about the primary bottlenecks that appear when scaling LLM inference to very long contexts.

canonicalClaims.claim: Long-context serving faces two linear-in-N pressures: per-token KV cache size (limiting batch capacity) and per-decode-step attention read bandwidth (rising vs the fixed weight-read baseline).
conditions: Standard full attention; no sparse or sliding-window approximation.
nonImplications: Does not imply mitigations do not exist (sparse attention, sliding window, KV quant).
Does not imply mitigations preserve quality.

misconceptions.claim: TPOT is independent of context length.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Attention reads scale linearly with context.

misconceptions.claim: Prefill time is independent of prompt length.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Prefill compute and I/O scale with prompt length.

misconceptions.claim: Increasing HBM alone is sufficient to serve arbitrarily long context.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Even with unlimited HBM, per-step attention bandwidth grows with N and eventually dominates.

implementationFacts: Common long-context mitigations: MQA/GQA, KV quantization, sliding window attention, sparse attention (Mamba-style or Mistral-style).
PagedAttention avoids per-sequence KV waste but does not change total KV bytes per token.
performanceScenarios: At 32K+ context and small batch, per-step attention time can exceed per-step weight time.
